heroHeadline: Ukraine 'Snow for Akhmat': 65 Chechen Drone Cadets Killed in Snizhne; Russian Overnight Strikes Kill 5, Injure 41; Russian Losses ~1.354M
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,548, Ukraine confirmed Operation 'Snow for Akhmat' — 11 drones armed with 100 kg warheads struck the Sever-Akhmat drone pilot training academy in Snizhne, Russian-occupied Donetsk Oblast, killing 65 Chechen cadets and their commanding officer Lt. Col. 'Buryi.' Simultaneously, Ukrainian forces struck a Russian FSB headquarters and an air defense installation — combined, Zelensky confirmed nearly 100 Russian personnel killed and wounded. Russian forces struck back overnight with combined drones and missiles, killing 5 Ukrainians and injuring 41 across multiple oblasts. Russian cumulative losses reached approximately 1,353,890 personnel as of May 22 — adding ~910/day to the May 21 figure. Mediazona's independent tracker continues to document Russian casualties by name. The twin aerial campaigns — Russia battering Ukrainian cities while Ukraine strikes Russian military training infrastructure and refineries deep inside Russian territory — define Day 1,548 heading into a pivotal summer 2026.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, France 24, NPR, CNN, NBC News, PBS, The Moscow Times, CGTN, Newsweek, Yahoo News, Kyiv Post, Euromaidan Press, EMPR Media, CNBC, Semafor, and Euronews. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
